Verses 2–4. “For he comes in like a refiner's fire and like fullers' soap; and he will sit smelting and purifying as silver and as gold; and he will purify the sons of Levi, and pour them out like gold and like silver; and they will bring to the Lord a sacrifice in righteousness; and the sacrifice of Judah in Jerusalem will please the Lord, as in the days of old and as in former years.” But there will be some gain, he says, from the punishment that will then be brought upon you. For like fire in a furnace refining silver and gold, or like soap cleansing clothing in the hands of fullers, he will, by the calamities then brought upon you, purify all who dare to exercise the priesthood unworthily; so that, chastened by the evils that befall them, they will from then on offer sacrifices to God as it is lawful to offer them to God who presides over justice, whose service it is fitting to fulfil with great fear, since he knows also how to punish those who choose to neglect him. Then indeed, he says, the Jews in Jerusalem will offer acceptable sacrifices to God, as in former times, when it was lawful for the righteous of each period, who attended to what was fitting, to offer their sacrifices. But neither “He will purify the sons of Levi” nor “The sacrifice of Judah in Jerusalem will please the Lord” will fit if anyone should think the words refer to the Lord Christ. For it was not only the sons of Levi who received cleansing then, but all people, to whom blessed Paul's saying applies: “Cleanse out the old leaven, so that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened.” Nor did the sacrifice of Judah in Jerusalem become acceptable to God then. On the contrary, every sacrifice of the law performed in Jerusalem ceased, being abolished together with the observance of the place, and there was revealed an ineffable and mystical sacrifice, which, in memory of the Lord's passion

and of the resurrection that followed it, we who have believed perform alike, not in Jerusalem but everywhere on earth. “Believe me, woman,” he says, “the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither in Jerusalem nor in this place.” And giving the reason, he says, “God is spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth; for the Father seeks such people to worship him.” He clearly shows that he has dismissed those who confined divine worship to Jerusalem and Samaria, but sets great value on these lovers of truth who everywhere on earth alike offer the sacrifice to God, the Maker of all, who is present everywhere alike.

These words were spoken fittingly of the time of the Maccabees. Then, because a great deal of wrongdoing was being committed both by those who were supposed to be serving as priests and by the people, God handed them over to war with the kings descended from the Macedonian succession, by whom they were beset with a great many evils. But when Judas Maccabeus and those with him stood up for the divine law and undertook war on its behalf against the Macedonian kings then reigning, a great change for the better came over the whole nation. For the Maccabees, having obtained divine help, defeated the kings, and after punishing the wicked among their own people, brought the whole nation into prosperity and good order, so that the divine laws prevailed among them, and all the lawlessness that had previously prevailed was driven out from them; and in particular the priesthood and all the service belonging to it were carried out as was fitting. This blessed Zechariah also made plain in his own words. This, then, is what he says here as well: Since you seek just judgment, a time will come when I will punish your offences; but having made you more sober through the evils that befall you, and having cleansed you of your old offences as in a furnace, I will bring you to attend to everything that pleases God, and in particular to make the offering of sacrifices in a way pleasing to God. Following this, since he had spoken of the gain from the punishment that would then be brought upon them, in order to offer his hearers a more complete correction, he speaks as follows:

Verses 5–7. “And I will draw near to you in judgment”—that is, I will then be [?] among you, judging what you do. “And I will be a swift witness against the sorcerers, and against the adulteresses, and against those who swear falsely by my name, and against those who defraud the hired worker of his wages, and who oppress widows and beat orphans, and those who pervert the judgment of the stranger, and those who do not fear me, says the Lord Almighty.” By this he shows for how many of the evils they then commit they will pay the penalty. “A swift witness” means: bringing swift punishment, as one who knows your affairs precisely. Upon all these, he says, and in short upon all who, neglecting the fear of me, have fearlessly attached themselves to what is worse, I will bring such punishment. Then he adds: “For I am the Lord your God,

and I have not changed; but you, sons of Jacob, do not keep away from the sins of your fathers; you turned aside from my statutes and did not keep them.” For I am always the same as myself, knowing when it is fitting to show forbearance and understanding the time for punishment; but you are exact imitators of your fathers' sins, turning aside from my laws just as they did and taking no account of keeping them, and for this you will receive just punishment.

Verses [7?]–10. The prophet then passes on to another offence, which they committed with regard to the firstfruits and tithes, being unwilling to render them according to the ordinance of the law. “Return to me, and I will return to you, says the Lord Almighty.” Turn toward me, he says, so that what comes from me may follow for you accordingly. “And you said, ‘In what shall we return?’” But you think, he says, that you need no turning at all; so unaware have you made yourselves of your turning away from me. “Will a man cheat God? For you are cheating me.” And you think this way, he says, supposing that you are deceiving me—and for human beings to attempt this against God is the height of folly and madness. “And you said, ‘In what have we cheated you?’” Yet even while doing this you have no perception of how outrageous it is. Then he names the sin: “Because the tithes and the firstfruits are with you; and you keep your eyes fixed on them; and you are cheating me.” For you do not bring the tithes and the firstfruits to the priests as prescribed, but keep them with yourselves. Then, thinking to secure some gain for yourselves this way, and looking to it as if to some very great profit, you are unwilling to deal sincerely with what you ought to render, but by offering a few cheap things you pretend to render what the law requires. This is nothing other than the conduct of people who think they can deceive me; for it would be deception not to discharge a lawful debt sincerely, but to try to be cunning in discharging it. Then he adds: “The year has been completed, and you have brought all the produce into the storehouses, and the plunder of the poor is in your houses.” For the year has reached its end, and the seasons of the year have completed their proper course according to my ordering, and from them came the yield of the crops. Then you, having gathered in the full harvest from the land, when you ought to have rendered thanks to God for it by offering the firstfruits and the tithes, did not do this; but having all but tossed a few small things to the priests, you brought everything into your own storehouses. You did not consider even this: that it differs in no way from plundering the food of the poor, for whose sake you have been commanded to give these things, so that both those who minister at the altar and those who because of poverty attend at my temple might obtain what they need. Following this he added:

Verses 11–12. “Turn, then, in this, says the Lord Almighty, and see whether I will not open the floodgates of heaven for you and pour out my blessing on you until you are satisfied; and I will set apart food for you, and I will not destroy the fruit of your land, nor will your vine in the field fail, says the Lord Almighty; and all the nations will call you blessed, because you will be a delightful land, says the Lord Almighty.” But change, he says, and correct these things, and you will see how I will give you abundant rain, and how I will give you abundance of crops to the full. For this is what “my blessing until you are satisfied” means: that you will have rich enjoyment of them. For “And I will set apart food for you” signifies this. And all your crops will be preserved undamaged, while the vine too will provide you its own rich enjoyment; so that, because of the plenty that prevails among you, all who are outside will call you blessed, because God has truly willed the best for you, so as to give your land the greatest abundance of crops beyond all others.

Verses 13–16. Then he goes back to his earlier words, as though judging the impious and wicked to deserve a second admonition, and says: “You have made your words heavy against me, says the Lord Almighty”—you have used harsh insults against me, he says. “And you said, ‘In what have we spoken against you?’” And then you have no perception of so great a blasphemy. For throughout, this prophet has put “you said,” as though reproaching them with great insensibility, with which they did outrageous things without having any perception of them, but were so disposed toward their own sins as not even to think they were sinning. Then he names the sin: “You said,” he says, “‘It is useless to serve God.’” For no benefit has come to us from taking care to keep what he commanded; nor did we gain anything more when we often prayed to him. Things have come to such a pass that we are in hardship and affliction, while we call others blessed who have taken no account of what pleases him; for them things go from good to better, though they always oppose him and suffer no harm from it. “These things those who fear the Lord spoke against him, each to his neighbour.” These things, he says, they did not hesitate to say to one another, those who pretended to have the fear of me more than all foreigners. God took note of them and left a record of them in writing for later generations, for the time when those who used such words and gave themselves over to every kind of lawlessness will pay the penalty, while every good thing will come to those who truly care for my laws. These I will judge worthy of my care at that time when I punish the wicked, choosing to treat them as my nearest and dearest and resolving to do everything best for them, as if someone were

so disposed toward his own son, who has always shown him great goodwill. Then he adds:

Verse 18. “And you will turn and see the difference between the righteous and the lawless, and between the one who serves God and the one who does not serve him.” Then the distinction will become plain between the righteous and the lawless, and between those who have been eager to serve God and those who refused to take any account of this, since the punishment brought upon the wicked and the good things that come to the right-minded will make the distinction clear [?] between those who are truly good and those who are truly evil. And he says these things too in keeping with what he said earlier about what would happen at the time of the Maccabees, when the wicked among the people received the heaviest punishment, while the lovers of the better obtained the greatest divine help in everything. Hence, in confirmation of what had been said, he adds:

Verses 1–2. “For behold, a day is coming, burning like an oven, and it will burn them up; and all the foreigners and all who do lawless things will be stubble; and the coming day will set them ablaze, says the Lord Almighty; and neither root nor branch of them will be left.” For at that time, he says, all the foreigners and the workers of lawlessness will be burned as by fire, destroyed like stubble by the punishment that falls upon them. This, then, is what he says about the wicked; and what to those who fear him? “But for you who fear my name the sun of righteousness will rise, with healing in its wings.” To you will come great splendour, justly granted you by God for your goodwill toward him; and he will rid you of every evil, sheltering you with his own care as with wings. And you will be, he says, no different from calves let loose from their bonds and leaping with great delight; for you will also prevail over the lawless, who will be like ashes under your feet, at that time no longer judged worthy of any care or correction. He says these things, as I have often said, of what happened at the time of the Maccabees, when God, granting his help, punished the wicked and established in ease and prosperity those who held fast to his statutes. These also punished and utterly overcame their adversaries, not only those among the foreigners but also those among their own people. From this it became clear to all how great the difference is between those who serve God and those whose mind is set the other way: the latter received the heaviest punishment, while the former were established in the greatest plenty and prosperity. This, then, was the form taken by the prophecy of blessed Malachi to the people, which he made about what concerned them both at that time and at the time of the Maccabees. But since he was the last of all the prophets who handed down their prophecies in writing, he thought it right next to show the abolition of the law, and to show what would come after it

…who would appear for the salvation of all people, who will put an end to the law and reveal his own perfection. You ought, then, to have believed in him at once, as soon as he first appeared, and to have recognized that he was the one whom Moses and all the prophets foretold: the one who would bring the law to its end and reveal the salvation common to all. That would have made it plain to everyone that this is the sum and the greatest good of the whole dispensation of the law: to bring all people to Christ the Lord, who would appear in his own time bringing such great blessings. But since you will show your own ingratitude even when he is revealed, the blessed Elijah will be sent to you before the second coming of Christ the Lord, which he will make from heaven. Elijah will unite those who had been divided from one another over religion. In particular, through the knowledge of true religion he will bring fathers into harmony with their children, though before they were divided over religion. In short, he will bring all people into one and the same union. Those who are still caught in impiety at that time will receive the knowledge of the truth from him, and so will also share in fellowship with the godly. God will do this because he cares for the salvation of all people, so that they may not remain in impiety and [?] his fearful coming, which will bring the utter destruction of the wicked.
